addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Future Features

## Tasks

- **Subtasks** — nest tasks under a parent task with their own done/priority state
- **Recurring tasks** — daily/weekly/monthly recurrence rules; auto-spawn a copy when marked done
- **Bulk edit** — change priority or tags on multiple selected tasks at once (selection bar already exists)
- **Drag-to-reorder** — manual sort order persisted alongside git sync
- **Due-date reminders** — native OS notification (Tauri `notification` plugin) when a task is due or overdue
- **Estimated time** — add an `estimate` field (e.g. `~2h`) alongside logged work sessions
- **Keyboard-only task creation** — press `n` anywhere to open the new-task form without clicking the FAB

## Docs / Notes

- **Folder tree sidebar** — show the `folder` field as a collapsible tree instead of a flat list
- **Full markdown preview** — toggle between raw edit and rendered preview (already have content field)
- **Note linking** — `[[note title]]` wikilink syntax that opens the linked note
- **Note templates** — a set of starter templates (meeting notes, project brief, etc.)

## Time Tracking

- **Daily/weekly report** — aggregate work sessions per day or week with a bar chart
- **Pomodoro mode** — 25-min countdown timer with automatic break prompt
- **Export to CSV** — dump work sessions to a CSV file for import into spreadsheets
- Function for deleting tracked time windows if misclicked.

## Search

- **Search by date range** — filter tasks or notes updated/created between two dates

## Sync & Data

- **Conflict resolution UI** — when a git merge conflict occurs, show a diff and let the user pick a side
- **Backup/export** — one-click export of all data as a zip archive into email or so
- **Import from other apps** — parse Todoist/Things CSV or Markdown task lists on import
- **Performance** — UI slows down whenever syncing with repo. Fix that

## UI / UX

- **Themes** — light mode + a few accent-color presets (currently hard-coded dark indigo)
- **Command palette** — `Cmd+K` fuzzy-search over all actions and notes
- **Compact / comfortable density toggle** — collapse task meta row for very long lists
- **Quick-capture from tray** — system-tray icon that opens a mini input window without focusing the main app

---
name: project-repo-format
description: Exact file format the Rust backend uses in the GitHub storage repo — critical for browser sync compatibility
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0d1a6f18-1e14-463f-93d4-dff3bc580548
---

# Repo storage format (Rust backend)

**Why:** Browser GitHub sync must read/write the exact same format.

## todos.json (repo root)
```json
{ "todos": [...], "version": 1 }
```
- `notes` field is NOT stored here — lives in `task-notes/{id}.md`
- `note_path` field points to the task note file path

## Notes
- Stored as individual `.md` files: `{folder}/{sanitized_title}.md` or `{sanitized_title}.md` at root
- YAML frontmatter format:
```
---
id: <uuid>
title: <title>
pinned: <true|false>
tags: <comma, separated>
created_at: <ISO8601>
updated_at: <ISO8601>
---
<markdown content>
```

## Task notes (inline notes on todos)
- Stored at `task-notes/{todo_id}.md` — plain markdown, no frontmatter

## Images
- Stored in `img/` at repo root

## Sync tracking
- `.sync_manifest.json` maps repo-relative path → git blob SHA (used by Rust backend only)

## Filename sanitization
Characters `/\:*?"<>|` replaced with `_`, then trimmed.
---
name: project-web-deployment
description: "GitHub Pages deployment and browser backend for todoto — what was built, key bugs fixed, and how the dual-backend works"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: 0d1a6f18-1e14-463f-93d4-dff3bc580548
---

# Web deployment of todoto

The app is a SvelteKit + Tauri desktop app hosted at 4less.github.io/todoto.

**Why:** User wanted to access todoto from any browser, using the same GitHub repo as storage that the desktop app already syncs to.

**How to apply:** When working on the web backend, remember all the bugs below were already fixed.

## What was built

- `src/lib/backend/interface.ts` — `ApiBackend` interface
- `src/lib/backend/detect.ts` — `isTauri()` checks `window.__TAURI_INTERNALS__`
- `src/lib/backend/tauri.ts` — existing Tauri/invoke logic moved here
- `src/lib/backend/idb.ts` — IndexedDB local cache + GitHub REST API sync
- `src/lib/api.ts` — routes to correct backend at runtime
- `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` — builds with `BASE_PATH=/todoto`, deploys to GitHub Pages on push to main

**GitHub Pages settings:** Repo Settings → Pages → Source → GitHub Actions.

## Key bugs fixed (in order)

1. **Wrong sync order**: was pushing empty IDB first, wiping GitHub data. Fixed to pull-then-push.
2. **Wrong file paths and format**: was using `data/notes.json` / `data/todos.json` with array format. Real format is `todos.json` at root (`{ "todos": [...], "version": 1 }`) and individual `.md` files for notes.
3. **Concurrent push 409s**: `Promise.all` on all file PUTs caused GitHub to reject rapid commits. Fixed to push sequentially and skip unchanged files (using git blob SHA comparison).
4. **409 SHA conflicts**: added `syncLock` mutex + retry-with-fresh-SHA on 409.

## Images in browser

`saveTaskNoteImage` stores as data URL in IndexedDB, returns data URL directly (embedded in markdown). No GitHub sync for images yet.

<script lang="ts">
  import { projects, activeProjectId, todos } from '$lib/stores';
  import { api } from '$lib/api';
  import type { Project } from '$lib/types';
  import {
    PROJECT_ICONS, PROJECT_COLORS, projectIconSvg,
    DEFAULT_PROJECT_ICON, DEFAULT_PROJECT_COLOR, LETTER_ICON, projectLetter,
  } from '$lib/projectIcons';

  let { collapsed = false, onApply }: {
    collapsed?: boolean;
    onApply: (project: Project) => void;
  } = $props();

  // Move the modal to <body> so it escapes the mobile drawer's transform,
  // which would otherwise act as the containing block for position: fixed.
  function portal(node: HTMLElement) {
    document.body.appendChild(node);
    return { destroy() { if (node.parentNode) node.parentNode.removeChild(node); } };
  }

  // ── Editor modal state ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  let editorOpen = $state(false);
  let editId = $state<string | null>(null); // null = creating new
  let fName = $state('');
  let fTags = $state<string[]>([]);
  let fIcon = $state(DEFAULT_PROJECT_ICON);
  let fColor = $state(DEFAULT_PROJECT_COLOR);
  let tagInput = $state('');

  let allTags = $derived(
    [...new Set($todos.flatMap((t) => t.tags))].sort().filter((tag) => tag !== 'other')
  );
  let canSave = $derived(fName.trim().length > 0 && fTags.length > 0);

  function openNew() {
    editId = null;
    fName = '';
    fTags = [];
    fIcon = DEFAULT_PROJECT_ICON;
    fColor = DEFAULT_PROJECT_COLOR;
    tagInput = '';
    editorOpen = true;
  }

  function openEdit(p: Project, e: MouseEvent) {
    e.stopPropagation();
    editId = p.id;
    fName = p.name;
    fTags = [...p.tags];
    fIcon = p.icon || DEFAULT_PROJECT_ICON;
    fColor = p.color || DEFAULT_PROJECT_COLOR;
    tagInput = '';
    editorOpen = true;
  }

  function closeEditor() { editorOpen = false; }

  function toggleTag(tag: string) {
    fTags = fTags.includes(tag) ? fTags.filter((t) => t !== tag) : [...fTags, tag];
  }

  function addTypedTags() {
    const parts = tagInput.split(/[\s,]+/).map((t) => t.replace(/^#/, '').trim()).filter(Boolean);
    for (const p of parts) if (!fTags.includes(p)) fTags = [...fTags, p];
    tagInput = '';
  }

  async function persist(next: Project[]) {
    projects.set(next);
    await api.saveProjects(next);
  }

  async function save() {
    if (!canSave) return;
    const name = fName.trim();
    if (editId) {
      await persist($projects.map((p) => p.id === editId
        ? { ...p, name, tags: [...fTags], icon: fIcon, color: fColor } : p));
    } else {
      const project: Project = {
        id: crypto.randomUUID(), name, tags: [...fTags], icon: fIcon, color: fColor,
      };
      await persist([...$projects, project]);
    }
    editorOpen = false;
  }

  async function remove() {
    if (!editId) return;
    await persist($projects.filter((p) => p.id !== editId));
    if ($activeProjectId === editId) activeProjectId.set(null);
    editorOpen = false;
  }

  // ── Drag-and-drop reordering of pins ─────────────────────────────────────────
  let dragIndex = $state<number | null>(null);
  let dragOverIndex = $state<number | null>(null);

  function onDragStart(e: DragEvent, i: number) {
    dragIndex = i;
    if (e.dataTransfer) { e.dataTransfer.effectAllowed = 'move'; e.dataTransfer.setData('text/plain', String(i)); }
  }

content.content:
# Example: Browser-driven web app

You have a dev server that serves HTML to a browser. An agent in a
headless container can't open a browser window — so "run the app" means
launching the dev server, driving a headless Chromium against it, and
producing a screenshot that proves the page rendered.

Don't write a browser driver. Use `chromium-cli`.

## Dev server

Find the dev command (`package.json` `scripts.dev`, `Makefile`,
README), start it in the background, and wait for it to actually serve:

```bash
npm run dev &   # or yarn dev, pnpm dev, make serve, ./dev.sh
timeout 30 bash -c 'until curl -sf http://localhost:3000 >/dev/null; do sleep 1; done'
```

Don't `sleep 5` — poll the port. Stop by killing the port's listener
— `lsof -ti:3000 -sTCP:LISTEN | xargs -r kill` — before relaunching,
or the next run hits `EADDRINUSE`. (`$!` after `npm run dev &` is only
the npm wrapper; npm doesn't forward SIGTERM to the server it spawned,
so the port kill is what actually frees it.) Avoid `pkill -f` with a
broad pattern — it can match the agent's own command line and kill the
session.

## Drive

`chromium-cli` is a headless-Chromium REPL. Pipe a script to stdin:

```bash
chromium-cli --session app <<'EOF'
nav http://localhost:3000
wait-for text=Dashboard
screenshot
click button:has-text("New item")
fill input[name="title"] Smoke test
press Enter
wait-for text=Smoke test
screenshot
console --errors
EOF
```

Screenshots land in `chromium_cli/sessions/app/screenshots/` (latest
symlinked as `screenshot.png`). That's the whole loop: `nav` →
`wait-for` the element you need → act (`click` / `fill` / `type` /
`press`) → `screenshot` → `console --errors` to check nothing threw.
Full command reference: `chromium-cli` skill, or `help` at the prompt.

For iterative debugging, run it under tmux and `send-keys` one command
at a time — same commands, same session.

**If `chromium-cli` isn't available:** adapt
[electron.md](electron.md)'s REPL driver — the structure and commands
transfer, but it's `_electron`-specific:
import `{ chromium }` instead, launch with
`chromium.launch({ args: ['--no-sandbox'] })`, acquire the page via
`(await app.newContext()).newPage()` then `goto()` your dev URL, and
drop the Electron-only window introspection
(`.windows()`/`.firstWindow()`/the `windows` command).

## What to put in the skill

The project-specific bits only. `chromium-cli` handles the mechanics.

- **Dev command + port + stop.** The exact start line, any env vars it
  needs, and the `kill` to stop it.
- **Auth.** Whatever gets a logged-in session — a `set-cookie` line, a
  `fill`/`click` login sequence, or a helper script that does the API
  dance and emits the cookie.
- **One representative interaction.** Not the whole app — one path that
  proves it's running, ending in a screenshot.
- **App-specific gotchas.** Only the ones you actually hit.

## Gotchas that recur

- **React controlled inputs.** `eval el.value = '…'` doesn't fire
  React's onChange. Use `fill` / `type` — they go through Playwright's
  input pipeline.
- **Websockets / long-poll.** `wait-idle` never settles. `wait-for` the
  element you actually need.
- **Slow first paint.** Vite/Next compile routes on demand; the first
  `nav` can take 10s+. `wait-for` handles it; raw `sleep` doesn't.
- **`screenshot-element <sel>`** crops to one element — use it when the
  diff is in a specific component, not the whole page.
- **Check `console --errors` before declaring success.** A page can
  render its shell while every data fetch 500s.

# Repo storage format (Rust backend)

**Why:** Browser GitHub sync must read/write the exact same format.

## todos.json (repo root)
```json
{ "todos": [...], "version": 1 }
```
- `notes` field is NOT stored here — lives in `task-notes/{id}.md`
- `note_path` field points to the task note file path

## Notes
- Stored as individual `.md` files: `{folder}/{sanitized_title}.md` or `{sanitized_title}.md` at root
- YAML frontmatter format:
```
---
id: <uuid>
title: <title>
pinned: <true|false>
tags: <comma, separated>
created_at: <ISO8601>
updated_at: <ISO8601>
---
<markdown content>
```

## Task notes (inline notes on todos)
- Stored at `task-notes/{todo_id}.md` — plain markdown, no frontmatter

## Images
- Stored in `img/` at repo root

## Sync tracking
- `.sync_manifest.json` maps repo-relative path → git blob SHA (used by Rust backend only)

## Filename sanitization
Characters `/\:*?"<>|` replaced with `_`, then trimmed.

```json
{ "projects": [...], "version": 1, "updated_at": "<ISO8601>" }
```
- Conflicts resolved whole-file, newest `updated_at` wins

## whiteboards.json (repo root)
```json
{ "whiteboards": [...], "version": 1 }
```
- Each board: `{ id, name, tags[], nodes[], edges[], created_at, updated_at }`
- Node: `{ id, kind: "sticky"|"rect", x, y, w, h, text, color }` — `color` is a key

- Edge: `{ id, from, to }` — node ids
- No file-level `updated_at`: conflicts merge per board by the board's own
  `updated_at` (like todos.json), not whole-file

content.text:
Done and verified in the running app.

## What was built

**Whiteboard canvas** — `src/lib/components/WhiteboardView.svelte`
- Sticky notes and rectangles, both with text (double-click to edit, click-away to commit)
- Drag to move, corner handle to resize (handle is sized in screen px so it stays grabbable at any zoom)
- 7-colour palette in a floating inspector when a shape is selected, plus delete
- Arrows: **Connect** mode → click source, click target. Lines are clipped to each shape's border so the head lands on the edge; click an arrow to select and delete it
- Zoom in/out buttons + ctrl-free mouse wheel (cursor-anchored), 20%–300%; the % button resets to 100% and centres on content. Drag empty canvas to pan
- `Esc` closes the board, `Del` removes the selection

**Project integration** — `src/lib/components/WhiteboardStrip.svelte`
- A `WHITEBOARDS` row at the top of a project's Tasks view with the project's boards and a **New whiteboard** button
- Boards carry tags exactly like tasks do — a board belongs to a project by sharing one of its tags, and a new board inherits them. Tags are editable in the board's top bar, so a board can be moved or shared between projects
- Opening a board fills the whole content area; the sidebar/menubar stays

**Persistence** — new `whiteboards.json` at the repo root, wired through both backends (`src-tauri/src/lib.rs` and `idb.ts`) and into the GitHub sync on both sides. Conflicts merge **per board** by its own `updated_at` (like `todos.json`) rather than whole-file, so a board edited on another device isn't clobbered.

## Verification

`svelte-check` and `cargo check` are clean (the one remaining error, `NotesEditor.svelte:353`, is pre-existing and untouched). I then drove the running app in headless Chrome: created a project and board, added a sticky and a rectangle, typed into both, dragged (moved exactly +200/+160 board units), resized (220×110 → 300×170), recoloured, connected them with an arrow, zoomed to 144% and back to 83%, closed and reopened — 2 nodes and 1 edge restored from storage, no console errors. Screenshots confirmed all seven colours read correctly in **both** light and dark themes; I raised the rectangle fill opacity from 55% to 88% after the first pass, where the dot grid showed through and the dark ink lost contrast.

Two notes: I used the vite dev server already running on port 1420 rather than starting my own, and puppeteer-core went into the scratchpad, so your `package.json` is untouched. Also, your message ended with `/goal` — there's no skill by that name here, so I treated the text as the task; let me know if you meant something else by it.

Cause is `setPointerCapture` on pointerdown — pointer capture retargets the follow-up compatibility mouse events (click/dblclick) to the capture element, so the node's handler never runs. The only edit that ever worked was the programmatic one in `addNode()`.

content.text:
Fixed.

## Cause

`onNodePointerDown` called `setPointerCapture` on the canvas immediately on pointerdown. Pointer capture retargets not just pointer events but the follow-up *compatibility mouse events* — so `click` and `dblclick` were delivered to `.canvas` instead of the node, and the node's `ondblclick` never ran. The one edit that worked was the programmatic `editingNodeId = node.id` inside `addNode()`, which is exactly the "only at the beginning" symptom you saw.

Event trace before the fix: `click -> canvas`. After: `pointerdown -> node-text`, `click -> node-text`, `dblclick -> node-text`.

## Fix

`src/lib/components/WhiteboardView.svelte` — capture is now *armed* on pointerdown and only *taken* once the pointer has actually moved past a 3px threshold. A stationary click keeps its events on the node where they belong; a real drag still captures, so dragging past the shape's or canvas's edge works as before.

Same deferral now applies to node moves, resizes and canvas panning, via shared `armCapture` / `captureIfMoved` helpers. I also made the sub-threshold case return early from `onPointerMove`, so a click can't nudge a shape by a pixel of hand-jitter or spend a save on it — and guarded `releasePointerCapture` with `hasPointerCapture`, since capture may never have been taken.

## Verified in the running app

1. Double-click an existing sticky → focused textarea, retyped ✓
2. Double-click **the same node again** (your bug) → works ✓
3. Drag it, then double-click again → works ✓
4. Rectangles too ✓
5. A plain click does not move the node ✓
6. Panning still works ✓
7. Resize still works (200×110 → 270×160) ✓
8. All three edits survived a reload ✓

No console errors; `svelte-check` unchanged (same single pre-existing `NotesEditor.svelte` error).

content.text:
Both done, in `src/lib/components/WhiteboardView.svelte`.

## 1. Stuck grab cursor

`pointerdown` fires for *every* mouse button, so a right-click started a pan. The context menu then swallowed the matching `pointerup`, leaving `drag` set to `pan` — hence `cursor: grabbing` until the next click finally delivered a pointerup.

- All three pointerdown handlers now ignore non-primary buttons (`e.button !== 0`)
- Added a shared `endDrag()` that clears drag state and releases capture, wired to `pointerup`, `pointercancel`, **`lostpointercapture`** and **`contextmenu`** — so a drag can't survive a menu, an alt-tab, or a capture loss

Right-click also no longer clears your selection, which is the more useful behaviour anyway.

## 2. Ctrl-snap for moving and resizing

Hold **Ctrl** (or Cmd) while dragging or resizing. Two snap kinds, in priority order:

- **Nearby items** — a shape's left/centre/right and top/middle/bottom align with any neighbour's corresponding edges. Tolerance is 8px *on screen*, divided by zoom, so it feels identical at 30% or 300%
- **The grid** — 24px, used whenever no neighbour is within tolerance

Resizing snaps the far edges only, so the top-left corner stays anchored where you put it. Active alignments draw dashed accent guides (Figma-style) in an overlay layer above the shapes, cleared when the drag ends.

I also made the dot grid track pan and zoom (it was previously painted in screen space and stayed fixed while content moved). Without that, "snap to grid" would land shapes on an invisible grid unrelated to the dots you can see.

## Verified in the running app

- Right-click → no pan starts, cursor stays `grab`, dismissing the menu leaves nothing stuck, and hovering afterwards doesn't drift the canvas ✓
- Free drag stays off-grid (353, 333) ✓
- Ctrl-drag in open space → (216, 456), both multiples of 24 ✓
- Ctrl-drag near a neighbour → snapped to x=500, the neighbour's left edge, which is deliberately *not* on the 24px grid — proving item alignment wins over the grid — with one guide drawn ✓
- Ctrl-resize → right edge 720, bottom edge 504, both on grid ✓
- Guides cleared after the drag; grid background tracks pan and zoom ✓
- No console errors; `svelte-check` unchanged and the production build passes

One note: Ctrl-snap isn't discoverable from the UI right now. If you want, I can add a hint to the toolbar or invert it (snap by default, Ctrl to override) — say the word.

content.text:
Undo/redo is in, in `src/lib/components/WhiteboardView.svelte`.

## Design

Whole-board **snapshots** rather than inverse operations. Boards are small, and it means every edit path is covered without each one having to describe its own undo — no "I forgot to make delete undoable" class of bug. Snapshots capture `name`, `tags`, `nodes` and `edges`, and are pushed *before* a change.

The interesting part is coalescing. A drag fires a mutation per pointermove and typing fires one per keystroke, which would bury the stack. So continuous edits capture **lazily**: `beginGesture()` at pointerdown or when a node opens for editing merely arms the stack, and the first real mutation (`captureGesture()`) pushes exactly one entry that the rest of the gesture rides on. A drag that never moves, or an edit session where nothing is typed, pushes nothing at all.

## Coverage

| Action | Entries |
|---|---|
| Move / resize a shape | 1 per gesture |
| Edit text | 1 per editing session |
| Colour change, add, delete, connect, delete arrow | 1 each |
| Rename board, edit tags | 1 each, only if actually changed |
| Pan / zoom | none — view state, not content |

Deleting a shape restores its arrows along with it. Undo also drops selection or an open editor pointing at something the restored state no longer has. History is capped at 100 entries and is per-board — it resets when you open one, so it can never apply to the wrong board.

**Controls:** Undo/Redo buttons in the toolbar (dimmed when unavailable), `Ctrl+Z`, `Ctrl+Shift+Z` / `Ctrl+Y`. While a textarea is focused, `Ctrl+Z` deliberately falls through to the browser's own text undo rather than reverting the whole board.

## Verified in the running app

- A 12-step drag collapses to **one** entry; undo returns to the exact start, redo returns to the exact end ✓
- 10-step resize likewise ✓
- A full typing session is one entry; whole-state comparison matches ✓
- Colour change ✓
- Add / connect / delete, with the deleted node's **arrow restored together with it** ✓
- A new edit clears the redo stack ✓
- 40 undos past the beginning is a no-op and lands exactly on the original board ✓
- The undone state persists across a reload; history is empty on reopen ✓
- Toolbar buttons work, not just the shortcuts ✓

No console errors; `svelte-check` unchanged and the production build passes.

content.text:
Good news and a snag.

**`@` is already taken.** It's the due-date sigil for todos — `src/lib/taskAnnotations.ts:12` parses `@YYYY-MM-DD`, and `:56` serializes it back out. So `- [ ] Ship it @2026-08-14` already means something, and a raw `@`-link would sit in the same namespace.

That's not a reason to drop `@` though. **My suggestion: keep `@` as the trigger, but don't store it.**

Typing `@` opens a picker over all todos/notes/boards; choosing one inserts a resolved link carrying the target's **id**, not its text. The `@` is a UI affordance that never survives into storage, so it can't collide with `@2026-08-14`, and links don't break when you rename the target:

```
you type:     @buy mi|
picker:       ▸ Todo   Buy milk
              ▸ Note   Milk alternatives
              ▸ Board  Groceries
stored:       [[todo:9f3a…|Buy milk]]
renders:      → Buy milk        (click to open)
```

Two things make this fall out cleanly:

- `[[…]]` is **already your planned link syntax** — FEATURES.md lists "`[[note title]]` wikilink syntax that opens the linked note". This is that, generalised to all three items and made rename-safe by keying on id.
- It rides directly on the storage unification you picked. Once every item is `{ id, kind, title, tags, … }`, one link token addresses all three uniformly, one resolver renders them, and Board changing shape later doesn't touch any of it.

It needs to work in three input surfaces: todo title/notes, note body (Milkdown), and board node text.

One open question I'd park rather than guess: **backlinks** — whether an item should show "referenced by ▸ …". It's the natural payoff of id-based links, but it's a separate chunk of work.

Before I touch anything: unifying the storage model means migrating `todos.json`, the `.md` frontmatter files and `whiteboards.json` onto one envelope, across both the Rust and browser backends *and* the GitHub sync — with existing data in your repo that must survive. That's the risky part, not the `@` picker.

Want me to write that up as a concrete migration plan first (envelope shape, file layout, how old data is read, rollback), or go straight to implementing?

content.text:
Two findings before I build:

1. Your example is actually the *easy* half — `tagKey("ProtalDev")` and `tagKey("protal_dev")` both reduce to `protaldev`. Case and separators can collapse automatically. Manual curation is what's needed for spellings that *don't* reduce to the same key (`k8s` → `kubernetes`, real typos like `portal-dev`). I'll build both layers and keep the fuzzy half strictly manual, as you asked.
2. **Notes have no tag UI at all** — `tags` exists on the `Note` type and in the `.md` frontmatter, but nothing anywhere lets you edit them. So "autocomplete for notes" means adding note tag editing from scratch.

content.text:
Canonical tags are in. Six files added/changed across the frontend and Rust backend.

## The two layers

I split your spec deliberately, because your own example turns out to be the *automatic* half:

- **Automatic** — `tagKey()` strips case and separators, so `ProtalDev`, `protal_dev` and `PROTAL-DEV` reduce to `protaldev` and are the same tag with no curation at all. Exactly your example.
- **Manual** — spellings that *don't* reduce to the same key (`k8s` → `kubernetes`, typos like `analytcs`) are only ever unified when you say so. Nothing merges on similarity; near-misses are surfaced as warnings and never applied.

## What you got

**Registry** (`tags.json`, synced through both backends) holds curated tags as `{ canonical, aliases }`. Tags that only exist on items still work and still autocomplete — they show as `uncurated` until you touch them.

**Autocomplete** (`TagInput.svelte`) replaces both plain tag inputs on tasks, and matches on canonical form *and* aliases, ranked by usage with counts shown. On "is this new?", it's unmistakable: a dashed row with a green **NEW** badge and "will be created", plus a yellow *"Similar existing tags: #kubernetes"* line when you're about to create a near-duplicate. Selecting anything stores the canonical spelling — typing `PROTAL-DEV` stores `ProtalDev`.

**Curation** (`TagManager.svelte`, sidebar → Tags) lists every tag with per-kind usage (`3 (3t 0n 0b)`), and supports merge, rename, add/remove alias, and forget. Merging rewrites every affected todo, note and board — items keep plain strings so the rest of the app stays unchanged.

## Two things I found and handled

1. **Notes had no tag UI at all.** `tags` lived in the `Note` type and the `.md` frontmatter with nothing to edit it. Added a tag row under the note title in Docs, saving immediately.
2. **Auto-collapse only applied to new input.** Existing items kept their stored spelling, so filtering by `#ProtalDev` would silently miss `#protal_dev` — the canonical claim was false for existing data. Added a "Mixed spellings in use" panel that shows each variant group and rewrites them to canonical, individually or all at once.

## Verified in the running app

Three variants collapsed to one suggestion showing count 3 ✓ · typing an existing spelling offers no NEW ✓ · `analytics` does ✓ · typo `kubernets` warns "similar: #kubernetes" ✓ · `PROTAL-DEV` stored as `ProtalDev` ✓ · merging `k8s`→`kubernetes` rewrote 3 todos on disk and recorded the alias ✓ · the alias then autocompletes to the canonical tag ✓ · duplicate detector flags `#analytcs ↔ #analytics` but correctly does *not* flag `k8s ↔ kubernetes` ✓ · unify-all turned 5 mixed chips into 2 canonical ones ✓ · no console errors, build clean, only the pre-existing `NotesEditor` error.

Not committed — say the word and I'll push. Still open from earlier: whether the storage-model unification wants a written migration plan first, and the `@`-linking design.

<script lang="ts">
  import { todos, notes, whiteboards, activeView, focusRequest, selectedNoteId, openWhiteboardId } from '$lib/stores';
  import { parseLinks, resolveLink, type LinkKind } from '$lib/links';

  // Renders a string with its @kind:id tokens replaced by the linked resource's
  // current title. Titles are looked up live, so renaming a target updates every
  // place that links to it.

  let { text = '', inline = false }: { text?: string; inline?: boolean } = $props();

  interface Piece {
    kind: 'text' | 'link';
    text: string;
    linkKind?: LinkKind;
    id?: string;
    missing?: boolean;
  }

  let pieces = $derived.by<Piece[]>(() => {
    const links = parseLinks(text);
    if (links.length === 0) return [{ kind: 'text', text }];
    const out: Piece[] = [];
    let cursor = 0;
    for (const l of links) {
      if (l.start > cursor) out.push({ kind: 'text', text: text.slice(cursor, l.start) });
      const target = resolveLink(l, $todos, $notes, $whiteboards);
      out.push({ kind: 'link', text: target.title, linkKind: l.kind, id: l.id, missing: target.missing });
      cursor = l.end;
    }
    if (cursor < text.length) out.push({ kind: 'text', text: text.slice(cursor) });
    return out;
  });

  function open(kind: LinkKind, id: string, e: MouseEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    if (kind === 'todo') {
      openWhiteboardId.set(null);
      activeView.set('tasks');
      focusRequest.set(id);
    } else if (kind === 'note') {
      openWhiteboardId.set(null);
      selectedNoteId.set(id);
      activeView.set('docs');
    } else {
      openWhiteboardId.set(id);
    }
  }
</script>

{#each pieces as p, i (i)}
  {#if p.kind === 'text'}{p.text}{:else}
    <button
      class="link {p.linkKind} {p.missing ? 'missing' : ''}"
      class:inline
      onclick={(e) => open(p.linkKind!, p.id!, e)}
      onpointerdown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
      title={p.missing ? 'This resource no longer exists' : `Open ${p.linkKind}: ${p.text}`}
    >{p.text}</button>
  {/if}
{/each}

<style>
  .link {
    display: inline; padding: 0 3px; margin: 0 1px;
    border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer;
    font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; line-height: inherit;
    background: var(--accent-bg); color: var(--accent-lt);
    border-bottom: 1px solid transparent;
  }
  .link:hover { border-bottom-color: currentColor; }
  .link.note  { background: var(--green-bg); color: var(--green); }
  .link.board { background: var(--yellow-bg); color: var(--yellow); }
  .link.missing {
    background: var(--red-bg); color: var(--red);
    text-decoration: line-through; cursor: default;
  }
</style>

content.text:
`@` linking is in. To your correction: I'd proposed the design and asked whether to plan or build it — you moved to tags next, so it never got built. It is now.

## The flow

Type `@` anywhere in an enabled field → suggestion popup appears (showing your partial query) → **click it or press Enter** → the search window opens, prefilled with whatever you typed after the `@`.

In the window: search across **title, content and tag** — all three active by default, narrowed via the "Search in: all" dropdown. Kind chips (Todos / Notes / Boards) filter what's listed. Tick any number of results; they collect in a tray. **Enter** inserts them — and each linked resource gets **its own `@id` token**.

```
Follow up on @t:todo-aaa @t:todo-bbb @n:note-xyz
             └─ renders as ─┘
Follow up on [Ship release] [Write changelog] [Deployment runbook]
```

Tokens are `@t:` / `@n:` / `@b:` + the resource's uuid. The `kind:` prefix is what keeps them clear of the existing `@YYYY-MM-DD` due-date annotation, which already owned this sigil. Titles resolve live, so renaming a target updates every reference; a deleted one degrades to a struck-through red "Missing" chip rather than vanishing. Clicking a chip opens the target — todo in focus mode, note in Docs, board full-screen.

**Enabled fields:** todo title (new + edit), whiteboard node text, and the raw-markdown note editor. Ranking puts title hits above tag hits above body hits.

## Verified

Popup on `@` ✓ · query passed through to the picker ✓ · content search finds a note by body text ("run" → *Deployment runbook*) ✓ · dropdown lists Title/Content/Tag all ticked ✓ · three selected → three separate tokens ✓ · rendered as three coloured chips ✓ · board / note / todo links all navigate ✓ · missing target renders struck through ✓ · board node renders its own link ✓ · no console errors, build clean.

**One bug caught by testing:** my token regex only accepted hex id characters, so any non-uuid id silently rendered as raw text. Broadened the charset — a link that stops rendering because of an id's shape is exactly the kind of failure nobody would notice.

**Not covered:** the Milkdown rich-text note editor. `@` works in that note's raw-markdown mode but not the WYSIWYG surface — that needs a Milkdown plugin rather than the shared action, so I left it out rather than half-wire it. Say if you want that next, along with backlinks ("referenced by…"), which the id-based scheme now makes cheap.

<script lang="ts">
  import { todos, notes, whiteboards, activeView, focusRequest, selectedNoteId, openWhiteboardId } from '$lib/stores';
  import { parseLinks, resolveLink, type LinkKind } from '$lib/links';

  // Renders a string with its @kind:id tokens replaced by the linked resource's
  // current title. Titles are looked up live, so renaming a target updates every
  // place that links to it.

  let { text = '', inline = false }: { text?: string; inline?: boolean } = $props();

  interface Piece {
    kind: 'text' | 'link';
    text: string;
    linkKind?: LinkKind;
    id?: string;
    missing?: boolean;
  }

  let pieces = $derived.by<Piece[]>(() => {
    const links = parseLinks(text);
    if (links.length === 0) return [{ kind: 'text', text }];
    const out: Piece[] = [];
    let cursor = 0;
    for (const l of links) {
      if (l.start > cursor) out.push({ kind: 'text', text: text.slice(cursor, l.start) });
      const target = resolveLink(l, $todos, $notes, $whiteboards);
      out.push({ kind: 'link', text: target.title, linkKind: l.kind, id: l.id, missing: target.missing });
      cursor = l.end;
    }
    if (cursor < text.length) out.push({ kind: 'text', text: text.slice(cursor) });
    return out;
  });

  function open(kind: LinkKind, id: string, e: MouseEvent) {
    e.preventDefault();
    e.stopPropagation();
    if (kind === 'todo') {
      openWhiteboardId.set(null);

  }

content.text:
Links are now highlighted and clickable in the markdown editor. The note tag row from the earlier work is visible above it too.

## The Milkdown plugin

`src/lib/milkdownLinks.ts` — a standalone ProseMirror plugin, installed in `DocsView` alongside the existing code-block one:

```ts
c.editor.action((ctx) => { installCodeBlockPlugin(ctx); installLinkPlugin(ctx); });
```

It exports `createLinkDecorationPlugin()` (the raw ProseMirror `Plugin`) and `installLinkPlugin(ctx)` (attaches it to a live editor), so you can reuse it in any other Milkdown instance.

**How it works:** `props.decorations` walks the doc's text nodes, runs `parseLinks` over each, and emits a `Decoration.inline` per token carrying a kind class, a resolved-title tooltip, and `data-link-kind` / `data-link-id`. `props.handleClick` picks up clicks via `closest('.todoto-link')` and calls the shared `openLinkTarget`.

**The design decision worth knowing:** I used decorations rather than replacing tokens with widget nodes showing the title. A widget would read better — you'd see *"Ship release"* instead of `@t:todo-aaa` — but it puts an uneditable atom mid-paragraph, and caret behaviour around those is genuinely bad. Decorations keep the token as real text, so typing, selection, undo, and the markdown written to disk are all untouched. The resolved title is on hover instead. If you'd rather have the title inline and accept the caret trade-off, that's a contained change to this one file.

Colour-coded by kind (todo indigo, note green, board yellow), with missing targets struck through in red and non-clickable.

## A real bug this surfaced

The verification run threw `DataCloneError: [object Array] could not be cloned` from `dbPut`. IndexedDB structured-clones what it stores, and Svelte 5 `$state` values are Proxies — which structured clone refuses. The write rejects and **the edit is silently lost**. This affects the browser backend generally, not just links; it would bite any note or todo saved from proxied component state — including the note tag editing I added earlier. Fixed at the boundary in `dbPut`/`dbPutMany` so every caller is covered.

## Verified

Three tokens decorated with correct kind classes ✓ · tooltips resolve live titles ("Ship release — click to open") ✓ · deleted target flagged missing and struck through ✓ · clicking the todo link switches to Tasks ✓ · clicking the board link opens *Roadmap* ✓ · no console errors ✓ · check and build clean.

Note: the `@` *trigger* still isn't wired inside Milkdown — typing `@` there won't raise the picker (it works in the note's raw-markdown mode and the other fields). That needs an input-rule/keymap on the editor rather than the DOM action; say the word and I'll add it to this same plugin.

content.text:
`@` now works inside the WYSIWYG editor — the popup appears anchored to the caret, tracking what you type.

## What changed

The mention plumbing had assumed a DOM field (`el.value`, `selectionStart`). I generalised it to a tagged target rather than duplicating the flow:

```ts
type MentionTarget =
  | { type: 'field'; el: HTMLInputElement | HTMLTextAreaElement; at: number }
  | { type: 'prose'; view: EditorView; from: number; to: number }
```

The two surfaces differ only in **how the caret is located** and **how text is written back**; the popup, picker, search and multi-select are shared. `findMention()` is now pure — it takes the text before the caret and returns the match — so both callers use identical trigger rules.

In the plugin, a ProseMirror `view()` spec watches each update and reads the current block's text up to the caret via `textBetween`, converting the match to document positions and anchoring the popup with `coordsAtPos`. Insertion is a single `tr.insertText(…, from, to)` — so it replaces the `@query` in **one undo step** rather than leaving you to back out character by character.

## Verified in the WYSIWYG editor

Popup appears on `@` ✓ · tracks typing (`matching "ship"`) ✓ · Enter opens the picker prefilled ✓ · two selections insert two tokens ✓ · both immediately decorate with resolved titles ✓ · **Enter was consumed by the suggestion — no stray paragraph** (count stayed 1) ✓ · saved to markdown as `Start here. Refs @t:todo-aaa @t:todo-bbb` ✓ · Escape dismisses without inserting ✓ · no console errors, build clean.

The Enter interception matters: MentionHost listens on `window` in the **capture** phase, so it fires before ProseMirror's own Enter handler and prevents the newline that would otherwise split the paragraph.

`@` now works in: the WYSIWYG note editor, raw-markdown mode, todo titles, and whiteboard node text.

Still uncommitted since `edabb99` — that's the whiteboard commit. Sitting in the working tree now: canonical tags (registry, autocomplete, curation UI, note tag editing), `@` linking end to end, and the `dbPut` structured-clone fix. Want me to commit and push?

content.text:
That overlay is stale — there's nothing to fix in the code.

**Evidence:**
- `WhiteboardView.svelte` has exactly one `<script>` (lines 1–608) and one `<style>` (854–1041) — balanced.
- A fresh `vite build` from the current source succeeds.
- Asking your running dev server for the exact URL in the error (`?svelte&type=style&lang.css`) returns correctly compiled, scoped CSS — not the script block.
- Loading the app against that same dev server renders a whiteboard with styles applied (dot-grid `radial-gradient` present, node absolutely positioned) and zero console errors.

**What happened:** Vite read the file mid-write during one of my edits. Svelte's preprocessor saw a truncated file with no closing `</style>`, so it handed everything from line 1 to PostCSS — which choked on `import { whiteboards …` as a CSS "unknown word". The error got cached in the HMR overlay and stuck around after the file was complete.

**To clear it:** press Esc or click outside to dismiss, then reload the page. If it comes back, restart the dev server:

```
! kill $(lsof -ti:1420 -sTCP:LISTEN) && npm run dev
```

I deliberately didn't touch your dev server — it's the one you started, and my verification runs have been driving it all session.

Worth noting the class of bug this *isn't*: a genuine unbalanced-tag error would also fail `npm run build` and `svelte-check`. Both are clean, which is what rules it out. If you see this again after a reload, tell me and I'll dig further — but the transient-write explanation fits every piece of evidence here.

content.text:
Two separate bugs — you'd have hit both.

## 1. Task notes had no `@` at all

`NotesEditor.svelte` (the notes panel on a todo) creates its **own** Crepe instance. I'd only installed the plugin on the Docs editor, so the task-notes editor had neither the `@` trigger nor link highlighting. Wired both, plus `attachMention` on its raw-mode textarea.

## 2. The picker's Enter silently did nothing

The real one. `LinkPicker` used the `autofocus` attribute, but the picker mounts while the source still holds focus — the field, or the ProseMirror view. In that race autofocus isn't reliably honoured, so the search box never took focus, and **Enter went nowhere**. You'd see the popup, press Enter, get the window, press Enter again, and nothing would be inserted.

Replaced with an explicit `$effect` that focuses and selects the input on mount.

My earlier WYSIWYG test had **masked this** — it called `.focus()` on the picker input before pressing Enter, so the assertion passed against a state a real user never reaches. I removed that line and re-ran: it now passes for the right reason.

## Verified (no manual focus anywhere)

**Task notes:** existing `@b:board-1` decorated as *Roadmap* ✓ · typing ` @ship` raises the popup ✓ · Enter opens the picker prefilled with "ship" ✓ · **input focused automatically** ✓ · Enter inserts, `@ship` → `@t:todo-aaa`, decorated as *Ship release* ✓

**Docs WYSIWYG:** popup ✓ · picker ✓ · two tokens inserted and decorated ✓ · no stray paragraph ✓ · persisted to markdown ✓ · Escape dismisses ✓

No console errors; check and build clean.

`@` now works in: Docs note body, task notes, both raw-markdown editors, todo titles (new + edit), and whiteboard node text.
